doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Touring the world and music as a universal language
summary: He has played in Europe, the Far East and Russia, where audiences respond to the music without language.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah I’ve been out here man, all these years. I’ve been all over the world. I’ve been to Europe about seven, eight, nine times. Been to the Far East about six times. Been to Russia about four or five times. All these different places. And I can’t say that I was able to get around and really maneuver in these places, but I’ve been there. I played there. Yeah.
Yeah. It’s pretty amazing that people around the world all respond to this American music.

Yeah. This is something. You can go to Russia and not be able to speak a word of Russian, but you get on that bandstand and you start playing, and people come right up, come right around the band, shaking your hand. And they’ll be talking and you don’t know what the hell they’re saying but they enjoy the music. The music pulls them in regardless of not being able to let’s say understand with each other what they are saying you know, but the music. And I always talk about that. Man, if you play the music, just play it. Play it right and you ain’t – you’ll never have any trouble. And you’d be surprised the people that you will enjoy, or will enjoy it with you. You know, because of the feeling of that music.
